source_quote:
Need framework picture here.
OK, we add framework picture for mooncake connector and mooncake layerwise connector
I think management sounds more like a feature similar to KV Pool, should we use a more percise word such as KV Transfer?
Thanks for the suggestion. Good point — "KV Transfer" is indeed more precise than "management." We'll update the description accordingly.
For consistency and readability, recommend standardizing to either Disaggregated Prefill (title case, space) or disaggregated_prefill (snake_case) throughout the document. The current section heading "Why disaggregated-prefill?" also mixes cases.
The phrase "The motivation is two-fold:" is redundant with the following bullet points. Consider removing it and directly starting with the two points for a cleaner structure.
The logical jump from "allows for better control over the system's TPOT" to "avoids the challenge of determining the optimal chunk size" is unclear.
Mathematical expressions can be changed into more understandable textual descriptions, such as "only supports scenarios where the TP degree of P nodes is an integer multiple of and greater than the TP degree of D nodes."
Maybe we should add planning support for DSA and Mamba.
Perhaps it could be expressed by adding an example TP table.
And Mooncake_connector now supports PCP/DCP, we should also add it to the chart.
Intuitively speaking, PD separation can enhance the overall system throughput.
Mooncake connector requires delay_free, but mooncake layerwise connector does not, it may also need to add.

The disaggregated-prefill feature enables efficient KV transfer of cache
across distributed nodes. This KV transfer allows for better control over
the system's TPOT (Time Per Output Token) and avoids the challenge of
determining the optimal chunk size.
